note: Letter and word counting. Every large language model is weak here because it sees tokens, not characters. Failures on this set are NOT evidence of a broken quant. Included precisely so that a real quant problem can be told apart from ordinary tokenizer weakness. One case here was wrong when first written: 'encyclopedia' has five standard vowels, not six, unless you count y. The model was right and the test was wrong. It is kept, with the y ambiguity spelled out in the prompt, as a reminder that a graded set is itself a thing that can be broken.

cases.q: How many times does the letter r appear in 'strawberry'? Number only.
How many times does the letter s appear in 'mississippi'? Number only.
How many times does the letter r appear in 'rhubarb'? Number only.
How many times does the letter a appear in 'banana'? Number only.
How many vowels (a, e, i, o, u only, not y) are in 'encyclopedia'? Number only.
How many times does the letter l appear in 'parallel'? Number only.
How many words are in this sentence: 'the cat sat on the mat'? Number only.
